title: kv-cache: improved memory management and eviction policies (fragmentation, paging, spillover)
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and lack of controlled spillover has been the root cause of several OOM incidents and degraded tail latency under mixed small/long-context workloads. This PR introduces a set of memory-management and eviction improvements: 1) slab-based allocator to reduce fragmentation across variable-sized KV entries; 2) a hybrid eviction policy (LRU + frequency-aware aging) with coarse-grained and per-slab eviction thresholds; 3) async paging/spillover to host DRAM (and optional local SSD) when GPU memory pressure crosses configurable watermarks; 4) on-GPU compaction pass for freeing fragmented regions without full cache rebuild; 5) operational knobs exposed via runtime config and CLI for tuning spill targets, watermark levels, and per-model quotas.

Changes are focused in the serving runtime's KV cache subsystem and the allocator, and include tests, benchmarks, and docs for operators. The description below summarizes rationale, design, tests, and rollout plan.

Design highlights: slab allocator: group KV entries into size classes to avoid internal fragmentation caused by many small prefix fragments; compaction: background compaction that coalesces free segments inside slabs when GPU SM idle detected; hybrid eviction: base LRU with frequency-aware promotions to avoid evicting short-lived but hot prefixes; paging/spillover: asynchronous spill to host DRAM via pinned-page transfers to avoid blocking token-serving threads, with fallbacks to local SSD for extended pressure; memory accounting: fine-grained per-model and per-route accounting and dynamic watermarks.

Operational/compatibility notes: defaults preserve current behavior for short term (feature gated). Spillover is disabled by default in hosted tier until further telemetry; Dedicated and Private customers can opt-in. Backwards-incompatible behavior avoided — eviction policy changes are gated by runtime flags and Linear tickets are linked for gradual rollout.

Performance: microbench results on mixed-chat+instruct load (1k concurrent connections, ~avg seq_len 1.2k) show: - 18% reduction in average GPU memory footprint under steady load - 45% reduction in fragmentation-related free-but-unusable memory in stress tests - 12% reduction in OOM incidents in the 72-hour soak test - 2.5% median latency regression at 99th percentile reduced to <0.5% after tuning eviction thresholds (see perf notes).

Testing: unit tests for allocator and eviction heuristics, end-to-end soak test harness updates, synthetic stress tests that reproduce fragmentation patterns, and new perf benchmarks included.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated. Start rollout to internal canary pool (perf-canary) for two weeks, observe memory and latency signals via Redwood Console dashboards added in this PR; then enable for Dedicated customers who opt-in, finally flip default for hosted after 4 weeks and monitored metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement slab allocator and compaction pass
- [x] Implement hybrid eviction policy and tuning knobs
- [x] Add async spillover path to host DRAM + optional local SSD
- [x] Unit tests and integration tests
- [x] Perf harness and benchmark results attached
- [x] Docs/CLI flags and runtime config changes

Related: ENG-1278 (kv cache stability), ENG-1305 (autoscaler memory signals), SUP-442 (customer incident for OOMs)

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: slab allocator, hybrid eviction, async spillover to host DRAM/SSD, background compaction. Feature gated; disabled by default for hosted at time of merge. Operators can tune via kv_cache runtime flags (docs/kv-cache-tuning.md).
